rationale: Rationale: The inductively-degenerated common-source topology with a tapped-capacitor load is selected for its excellent noise performance and inherent bandwidth control, critical for the NF ≤ 1.8 dB target at GPS L1. The series inductor (Lg) at the gate provides impedance matching to 50Ω through resonant tuning, satisfying S11 ≤ -12 dB without requiring additional matching components. The degeneration inductor (Ls) enhances input match by reducing the real part of the input impedance and improves linearity. The tapped capacitor load (Ct1, Ct2) forms a high-Q resonant network with Ld, enabling high gain (S21 ≥ 16 dB) at 1.575 GHz with minimal current consumption. The topology is inherently low-power, scalable to 3 mA Idd, and leverages the 45nm process's low parasitics to maintain stability and noise figure performance. Its differential-free, single-ended structure aligns with the device budget and avoids floating nodes.
